original.target_description: Experiment 2A: mediation of information condition effects on perceived likelihood of partner detecting a lie by feeling of knowing the partner; restricted to participants who believed they were connected to another participant.

es.location: Supplementary Information, p. 3, A.2 Experiments 2A-B, Additional results
es.quote: And we again find that participants’ feeling of knowing their partner significantly mediated the effect of information on participants’ beliefs that their partners would detect their lies (indirect effect = 4.18, bias-corrected 95% confidence interval = [1.64, 7.35]).

p.location: Supplementary Information, p. 3, A.2 Experiments 2A-B, Additional results
p.quote: And we again find that participants’ feeling of knowing their partner significantly mediated the effect of information on participants’ beliefs that their partners would detect their lies (indirect effect = 4.18, bias-corrected 95% confidence interval = [1.64, 7.35]).

notes: Only assigned unfinished original es and p fields were examined; all other fields are placeholders. Canonical source identifies the title and authors and is the primary Supplementary Information. The restricted-sample mediation is explicitly reported as indirect effect = 4.18 with bias-corrected 95% CI [1.64, 7.35]. The source does not explicitly label this estimate as an unstandardized b; retain the printed metric, indirect effect. No numeric p or p bound is printed for this mediation; the statement significantly mediated does not supply a numeric p bound. The adjacent P = .008 and P < .001 refer to separate condition-comparison t-tests and are not assigned to this mediation. No PDF was supplied. No N extraction or calculation was assigned.
